Japan’s trade deficit widened to JPY 1,105.6B in August from JPY 294.1B a year earlier, marking the fourth consecutive monthly deficit and the largest since January.
Imports jumped 28.0% year over year to JPY 11,153.9B, exceeding the 26.3% market forecast and marking their strongest growth since November 2022.
Crude oil import value surged 58.7%, pushing up Japan’s energy bill amid higher oil prices and Middle East supply disruptions.
Exports rose 19.3% to JPY 10,048.4B, beating expectations for an 18.2% increase and extending their growth streak to 12 months.
Semiconductor-related shipments remained a key export driver, while exports to the U.S. rose 24.9% and those to China increased 20.6%.

title: Japan’s August trade deficit widens sharply on higher imports
